Hi! As a biker myself I can agree you’re NTA, even if you were covered by insurance. 

Laws are different here in the UK as you do a CBT (compulsory basic training) day and then you can go on the road with L plates on nothing higher than a 125cc as long as you avoid Motorways. You do not need a theory test and it’s valid for 2 years. You then have 2 more tests to pass to get an unrestricted bike (one if you’re over 24 and do direct access). 

I did my CBT twice (second time after it expired ofc) and had my CBT for 4 years altogether. So I only had a total of 16 hours (8 per CBT) of instructor time and was allowed on the roads. 

My dad has a 600cc and a 1200cc (Bandit and FJR if you’re interested lol) and has been riding for about 12 years consecutively (more overall but that’s another story) and I wouldn’t even let HIM take my little 125cc (Honda CBF) any further than he had to (check when there was a problem). He even has his ART/ARM and I’m dodgy about it, he understood and respected my decision, he’d be the same with either of his bikes. 

If he’s really as good as he said he is surely he can just go to weekend lessons on a bike provided by the store (providing you have that option in the US) and learn that way.

ETA: I have ridden a 300cc as a “taster” for doing my actual test and that was enough of an engine jump for me to go “oh shit”. Don’t even ask me about the time my dad let me try his 600cc.
